recipes.name: Maui Girl's Mango Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon butter, cut into small chunks

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Line a 9-inch pie pan with half of the pie pastry. Set aside.

Combine mango, sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, and cinnamon in a bowl; stir until the sugar has dissolved. Transfer mango mixture into the prepared pie pan. Dot the mixture with the butter, then cover with the top crust. Pinch the edges of the top and bottom crusts together to seal. Cut several vents on the top crust.
Bake in the preheated oven until the crust is golden brown and the juices are bubbling, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Maui Girl's Mango Pie
raw_recipe.description: If you like peach pie, you will love this dreamy tropical pie. It has a brighter flavor with the added beauty of this luscious island fruit.

review.reviewBody: Lovely pie and easy to put together! Make sure to taste your mangoes before adjustig the sugar. I used champagne mangoes (all I had) and omitted the lemon just because I felt it didn't need any. I made this into a single serving (1 cup mangoes) for my daughter using a remekin and made French Pastry Pie Crust (AR). I think this would be a perfect summer pie, cooled, and have it with an ice cream.

Wonderful pie! Thank you for the recipe. My touch as follows: I added 1 extra teaspoon of cinnamon, and extra 1/2 cup of sugar, and extra butter pieces. I I used two 9 oz Graham crackers pie shells. I poured filling in one and crumbled the extra pie crust in tiny pieces over the pie to cover entirely. I baked at 400 for 1 hour and 15 min covered with foil paper. I took off the foil leaving the pie edged covered the last 15 mins. I let cool at room temperature for one hour and refrigerated over night to set the consistency. It turned out perfect. I served warm with vanilla ice cream. My picky husband loved it! And he does not like any type of cobbler. This pie was a huge hit!! I will definitely make again!

Wonderful recipe with some adjustments - I did a mix of 2/3 mango and 1/3 peach since both of them were in season at the time. Changed the 1/2 cup white sugar to half and half brown sugar to white sugar and doubled the cinnamon. Also added a tablespoon of vanilla. For the pie crust I made Ruth’s Grandma’s pie crust recipe from this site. After a simple egg wash with sugar sprinkle on top it baked up beautifully - and was a complete hit.

As others have said, it is indeed similar to peach pie. The colour and flavour are brighter, though.

I didn't have cornstarch so I used 6 tablespoons of arrowroot powder. Worked perfectly. 

It was runny while hot, but set up beautifully as it cooled.

Definitely want to make this recipe again.

loved the pie several times now. My last iteration I added 1/8 teaspoon each of nutmeg and cloves. Really made the flavor pop! I'm in Kenya, where mangos are between ten and thirty cents each while apples are hard to get.
I made this recipe and made one of the adjustment. I put a half a cup of shredded coconut for texture and for tropical taste. My husband was absolutely in love with his pie.?

My husband loved the pie. I used frozen mangos, but since I only had about 2 cups I added 1.5 cups of frozen mixed berries, leaving all other measurements for sugar, corn starch, lemon, and cinnamon the same. The result was a cross between a tart cherry pie and sweet apple pie--for him a perfect balance. The mango pieces were described as tasting like a peach. I cannot try the pie since it is gluten, but I look forward to making this pie again with a gluten-free crust and only mangoes.

Reduced sugar to 1/4 cup. Made a Crisco crust recipe, 2/3 Crisco and 1/3 butter. Turned out d__n near perfect.
Thanks Mango Mama!

The first time I made this, I followed the recipe exactly. It did taste way too close to apple pie. I had a hunch it was the cinnamon that was responsible for this phenomenon. So the second time, I used just a small shake of cinnamon, maybe equal to a couple of pinches, and that did the trick! The glorious taste of those sunny mangoes was able to shine through, and the whisper of cinnamon, while it can't be identified, enhances and underscores the natural sweetness and nuanced flavor mangoes bring to your table. If you make that one, simple change, and you adore mangoes like we do, you will love this. Promise.

I didn't make any changes. I did use the cup trick(halve the mango. Slide a glass along the inside of the skin to get one whole side of mango. It slips into the glass with no mess). it's a delicious recipe.
Very popular in my family, I was short mangoes one day and supplemented with peaches, delicious. I have also topped with raspberries instead of a crust.
Added some ground cloves and nutmeg, yummy!

First time making this pie as mango season is crazy this season. It turned out amazing, the flaw as interesting though, it was delicious but the strong mango flavour was altered which I think was the cinnamon. Other than that, I will make it again !
I made this and everybody loved it, so simple and easy to follow recipe and instruction.

This pie is one of the first things I make each year when mangoes start falling off of the tree. My family and my friends all look forward to it, and my friends are more than happy to supply me with mangoes from their trees (I don’t have one, but I always get more mangoes than I can use). The flavor is delicious, especially with really good mangoes right from the tree. I use King Arthur Flour’s double crust recipe, and we can hardly wait for it to cool down, and I make several for my friends, as well. Fabulous pie.

Third time making this recipe using tender flake deep dish pie shells. It turns out great every time. I have added some rehydrated apricot which I chop up and add to mixture and one time added coconut.
This will be one of my favorites!

It was quite good, but you couldn't really tell the mango flavor. It just tasted like a fruit pie. I used the big gree/redish mangoes maybe using Ataulfo or other stronger mangoes will be better. Overall it was delicious though! Will definitely keep making it!
Made as written. Loved it! Waited till is was barely warm before cutting. Added cool whip to the top when I served it.
This is my absolute favourite pie.
